analysis.title: GS Lin - Prime Perspective: AI Unwinds 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: Global equities were significantly net sold on Oct 14 (-2.1 SDs vs 1-year), with long sales outpacing short sales about 3 to 1, a risk unwind rather than a short-selling episode.

Nearly all major regions were net sold, led by North America (long-and-short sales) and EM Asia (long sales > short covers). Korea and Taiwan were the most net sold Asian markets, driven by long sales, and foreign investors were significant net sellers in both overnight on Oct 15.
US equities were 66% of global net selling (-1.8 SDs vs 1-year), with long-and-short sales at 1.9 to 1. Single stocks and macro products made up 54%/46% of the dollar net selling.
8 of 11 US sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech and Industrials. Health Care and Staples were the most net bought, which the desk reads as an incrementally defensive posture.
All US Info Tech subsectors were net sold, led by Software (short-and-long sales), Semis & Semi Equip (long sales) and, to a lesser extent, IT Services (long sales).
Global AI stocks (GSXGGLAI constituents) saw the second-largest net selling of the past year after July (-2.8 Z score), with long-and-short sales at 3.5 to 1.
Hedge funds net sold Global AI stocks for five consecutive sessions (Oct 8-14). All cumulative hedge fund net buying in the group since the start of 2025 has now been reversed.

Net allocation to Global AI stocks is 26.1% of total global single stock net MV, down from a 31.7% peak in early June. That is the 49th percentile vs the past year and the 83rd percentile vs the past three years.
The aggregate long/short ratio across Global AI stocks is 3.27, down from a 4.34 peak in early June. That is the 7th percentile vs the past year and the 64th percentile vs the past three years.

Hedge fund net leverage fell 1.5 pts on the day and 4.3 pts MTD to 73.3%, the 6th percentile vs the past year. Gross leverage is 310.3%, the 72nd/91st/94th percentile vs 1/3/5 years, so gross remains high while net is low.

Global fundamental L/S managers fell 0.9% on Oct 14, mainly on beta losses, and are down 2.1% MTD but up 10.5% YTD. TMT L/S managers fell 2.7% and are down 4.5% MTD. Asia-focused L/S managers fell 0.9% and are down 4.1% MTD but up 19.3% YTD, versus a roughly +40% YTD peak in late June. Global systematics rose 0.5% and are up 21.7% YTD.

Staples were among the most net bought US sectors on Oct 14, alongside Health Care, consistent with a defensive shift. This is a flow observation, not a formal rating.

risk_factors: AI unwind: five straight sessions of hedge fund net selling in Global AI stocks, with the Oct 14 net selling the second largest of the past year after July.
Gross leverage remains at the 91st/94th percentile vs 3/5 years while net leverage is at a 1-year low percentile, so a high-gross, low-net book is exposed to further de-risking.
Heavy foreign net selling in Taiwan and Korea overnight on Oct 15 points to continued pressure in Asian tech-linked markets.
Asia L/S managers are down 4.1% MTD and TMT L/S managers are down 4.5% MTD, so further drawdowns could force more selling.
